title: Adjoining a radical with nonpower residue
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$, uniformizer $t$, and residue field $k=R/(t)$ of characteristic $p$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $a\in R$ have residue $\bar a\notin\{x^p:x\in k\}$. In a field extension choose $z$ with $z^p=a$ and put $E=F(z)$. Then $[E:F]=p$ and the integral closure of $R$ in $E$ is $R[z]$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. This ring is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $t$, and its residue field is $k[\bar z]\simeq k[T]/(T^p-\bar a)$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. No completeness or characteristic assumption on $F$ is required.

source.place: Tag 09EX, lemma-pre-purely-inseparable-case, with its residue-field identification from the monic root presentation.

proof.text: Put $f=T^p-a$, $C=R[T]/(f)$, and $x=[T]$. Since $p>0$, $f$ is monic of degree $p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], $C$ is free over $R$ on $1,x,\ldots,x^{p-1}$ and $C/tC\cong k[T]/(T^p-\bar a)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-x-pow-p-minus-t-irreducible], the polynomial $T^p-\bar a$ is irreducible: here the field is $k$, of characteristic $p$, and the nonpower hypothesis is exactly the assumption on $\bar a$. By [lem-trf-irreducible-polynomial-quotient-field], this quotient is a nonzero field. Thus $tC$ is a maximal ideal. The free basis also shows that the coefficient map $R\to C$ is injective and multiplication by $t$ on $C$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 09EX, lemma-pre-purely-inseparable-case, omitted proof: monic root algebra and residue polynomial; Fields Tags 09HF and 09FI.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], the finite $R$-algebra $C$ is integral over $R$. For any maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $C$, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal] says that its contraction is maximal in $R$, hence equals $tR$. Therefore $tC\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Since $tC$ is already maximal, $\mathfrak n=tC$. Thus $C$ is local with unique maximal ideal $tC$.

proof.text: Evaluation at $z$ gives a unital homomorphism $C\to\Omega$, where $\Omega$ is the field extension containing $z$. It is injective: a nonzero $c=t^m d$ from step 3 maps to a product of the nonzero image of $t^m$ and the invertible image of $d$. Its image is exactly $R[z]$, so identify $C=R[z]$ inside $\Omega$. Every element of $F[z]$ is $c/b$ with $c\in C$, $0\ne b\in R$, by taking a common denominator of its finitely many coefficients. If $c\ne0$, write $c=t^m d$ as above; then $(c/b)^{-1}=b t^{-m}d^{-1}\in F[z]$. Hence $F[z]$ is a field, so $F[z]=F(z)=E$ and $E$ is the fraction field of $C$. The powers $1,z,\ldots,z^{p-1}$ span $E$ over $F$ by $z^p=a$, and are independent: multiply any $F$-linear relation by a common nonzero denominator in $R$ and use the injectivity and free basis from step 1. Therefore $[E:F]=p$.

proof.text: For any nonzero ideal $J$ of $C$, choose a nonzero element $c\in J$ whose exponent $m$ in step 3 is least. Since $c=t^m d$ with $d$ a unit, $t^m\in J$. Every other nonzero element of $J$ has exponent at least $m$ and hence belongs to $t^mC$. Thus $J=t^mC$; the zero ideal is principal too. As a subring of $\Omega$, $C$ is a domain. It is local by step 2 and is not a field, since its maximal ideal $tC$ is proper and contains the nonzero element $t$. It is therefore a DVR by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with uniformizer $t$. The identification in step 1 is its residue field, sending $[T]$ to the residue $\bar z$ of $z$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), explicit principal-ideal argument; applied to Tag 09EX.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], the principal ideal domain $C$ is integrally closed in its fraction field $E$. Every element of $C$ is integral over $R$ by step 2. Conversely, if $v\in E$ is integral over $R$, its same monic equation is an equation over $C$, since $R\subseteq C$; integral closedness gives $v\in C$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], $C=R[z]$ is exactly the integral closure of $R$ in $E$. Only the residue field $k$ was assumed to have characteristic $p$; none of the constructions or arguments used completeness of $R$ or a characteristic condition on $F$.

This is the first split of an unsplit statement (not a re-split), with zero new nodes and six steps. All ten cited nodes are pre-existing Mathlib leaves; I checked each statement and its hypotheses. Source: Stacks more-algebra.tex l.34663, Tag 09EX, whose proof is 'This lemma proves itself'. The item matches it and is not weakened ([E:F]=p is equivalent to a not being a pth power; uniformizer t means weakly unramified). Steps: (1) C=R[T]/(T^p-a) is free and C/tC=k[T]/(T^p-ā); this is irreducible over k because k has char p and ā is not a pth power, so it is a field and tC is maximal. (2) C is integral over R and maximal ideals contract to tR, so C is local. (3) Factoring out the minimal t-power of the coefficients leaves a unit coefficient, so every nonzero element is t^m times a unit. (4) Evaluation at z is injective, F[z] is a field, and [E:F]=p. Step 4 says the injectivity used there comes 'from step 1', but it is the evaluation injectivity proved in step 4 itself; this is harmless wording. (5) Every ideal is t^mC, so C is a DVR with residue field from step 1. (6) A PID is normal, which gives the integral closure. Small cases checked: p=2 with F_2(u)[t]_(t), a=u; mixed characteristic Z[U]_(p); ā=0 or a pth power excluded (a=1 fails as it should). Batch-5: lem-trf-irreducible-polynomial-quotient-field is a Mathlib leaf of general algebra (F[T]/(irreducible) is a field). It is not part of the trace formula, Poincaré duality or their proofs, so it is accepted. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, there is no SGA citation, the blueprint chain is unchanged, and there are no tool_uses.
